predecessors.name: Spanish Florida
predecessors.text: the Florida panhandle west of the Apalachicola, Pensacola and its district, ceded by Spain

predecessors.name: New France
predecessors.text: the Gulf coast of Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana east of the Mississippi: Mobile and the Florida Parishes, ceded by France

successors.name: Spanish Florida
successors.text: West Florida without Baton Rouge, Fort Bute and Mobile: the Pensacola district

ledger.x: 1763: the Gulf coast from the Mobile to the Mississippi, ceded by France in the treaty signed on 10 February 1763 and attached to West Florida by the proclamation of October 1763 (the month is the proclamation's).
1779: Fort Bute and Baton Rouge fall to Spain ('the remaining British forces surrendered following the Battle of Baton Rouge').
1781: the fighting for West Florida ends at Pensacola on 10 May 1781.
1781: British West Florida ends in fact with the surrender of Pensacola; the Peace of Paris (1783) formally had Great Britain cede 'the territories of West Florida and East Florida back to Spain'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of British West Florida
wars.outcome: Gálvez took Fort Bute and Baton Rouge in September 1779, Mobile on 14 March 1780 and Pensacola on 10 May 1781; the Peace of Paris (1783) ceded West Florida and East Florida to Spain.

certainty.note: No survey on the pages: the northern limit (31 N, later extended according to other sources) and the eastern limit at the Apalachicola are approximate.
